name: HI-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strongly Democratic district with a +13 partisan lean
Incumbent Ed Case running with a large fundraising edge
No general-election polling or expert ratings available
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~95%
model.rationale: Ed Case holds a Honolulu-based seat that leans Democratic by 13 points, and he has raised over $1 million while his Republican opponent reports no fundraising. Markets price a Democratic win around 95%, and the fundamentals point to a margin in the low twenties.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a closer race or unexpected outside spending against Case would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Hawaii's first district is a solidly Democratic seat, and incumbent Ed Case is seeking another term with the advantages of incumbency and a clear financial edge. His Republican opponent, Adriel Lam, has reported no fundraising, and minor-party and independent candidates are also on the ballot.

There are no public general-election polls and no expert ratings for this race, so the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, Case's incumbency, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at roughly 95%. A comfortable Democratic margin in the low twenties is the most likely outcome.
